note: Synthetic voice reading one passage with deliberate, known flaws. Word timings are exact by construction; Whisper and WhisperX were replaced by stand-ins. Every other number comes from the real analysis code.
selection_note: Each sample is the first generated take (seeds from 200 upward) that fits its description: the clean take has no flag; each flawed take has its injected flaws detected, with at most 2 additional detections. The samples illustrate the interface; they are not a measurement of detection accuracy.

diagnostics.comment: How many clean synthetic takes (same generator, no flaw) the current, uncalibrated thresholds flagged. Calibration on real recordings has to bring this down.

passage.title: Project talk (demo passage)
passage.text: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Over the past year our team has built a tool that helps people improve the way they speak. It listens to a recording, compares it with a clear example of the same message, and shows exactly where the delivery changed. For instance, you might speak too quickly during a key point, or pause for too long before an answer. The tool marks those moments on a timeline, explains what it measured, and suggests one simple change. We tested it with students, teachers, and engineers, and most of them improved within a single week. Today I will show you how it works, step by step. Please feel free to ask questions at any time.

samples.title: Clean delivery
samples.description: A control take: the same voice reading the passage at its normal pace, with no deliberate flaw. It shows what the dashboard looks like when nothing is flagged.

samples.title: Rushed explanation
samples.description: The third sentence is read about 1.8 times faster than the baseline pace; everything else is normal.

samples.title: Hesitant delivery
samples.description: A 1.9 s silence inside a phrase in the fourth sentence, and the sixth sentence read at about 0.6 times the normal speed.

samples.title: Mixed flaws
samples.description: Three deliberate flaws in one take: a fast second sentence, a 3.2 s silence between two sentences, and a seventh sentence 20 dB quieter.
